title: sd-review routing policy
description: Policy for `bin/sd-review`, read from `.github/sd-review.json`. JSON, not YAML or TOML, per decision D-C1: PyYAML is not stdlib and tomllib is absent from the 3.9 interpreter at /usr/bin/python3. Every key is optional; an absent key takes the built-in default documented in `DEFAULT_POLICY` in `bin/sd-review`. An absent FILE means the whole built-in default is used. A file that exists and is malformed is an error, never a silent fall back: the author who wrote it meant it. The routing rules themselves are not configurable -- they live in the pure function `route()` in `bin/sd_route.py` and are the same in every repository; this file only supplies the data that function reads.

$schema.description: Path or URL to this schema. Ignored by the reader.

tier_order.description: Review tiers from cheapest to most expensive. Escalation moves one step to the right and stops at the end; `skip` must be first if the repository wants a free tier at all. Names must be unique.

tiers.description: Which backends each tier chains, in order. Every key must appear in `tier_order` and every backend named must exist in the backend table in `bin/sd-review`; a typo is rejected at load time rather than silently reducing the providers a change is reviewed by. A tier missing from this object chains nothing.

default_tier.description: The tier a change starts at when no category matches. Must be one of `tier_order`.

categories.description: Path-shaped classes of change, matched required-first: a category with `required: true` outranks any non-required one no matter which order they appear in. The first match names the starting tier.

tier.description: Starting tier for this category. Must be one of `tier_order`.

required.description: Match this category before any non-required one.

docs_skip.description: Allow-list: a change whose EVERY path matches one of these globs plans `skip`. Safe to widen, because `never_skip` is checked first and always wins.

never_skip.description: Deny-list: any path matching one of these globs removes `skip` from the table for that change, whatever `docs_skip` says. This is the non-removable half of the pair -- it is why a repository can declare documentation free and still keep one directory inside it reviewed.

sensitive.description: Globs whose presence escalates the tier one step. Workflow files, credentials handling, and installers are the usual entries.

large_change_lines.description: Added-plus-removed lines above which the tier escalates one step. Default 800.

authors.description: GitHub logins this repository's framework rules hard-fail for in CI (R10-D5). Everyone else gets a reporting, passing check, so a collaborator who has not adopted the framework can never be blocked by it. The local review lane reads this list and reports it; it is the CI lane, installed separately by `sd-review setup-github`, that acts on it.

severity_floor.description: The severity at which a finding is dispositioned `blocking` rather than `advisory`, and therefore the severity at which `sd-review` exits 1. Findings are dispositioned locally and are never posted anywhere; this only decides how the local run reports them. Default `medium`.

challenge_providers.description: Backends added to the front of the chain when `--challenge` is passed. They are added to the tier's chain, not substituted for it: a challenge run is an extra stance, not a cheaper review.

planning_providers.description: Backends added to the front of the chain for `--scope planning`. Defaults to `codex`, which is the designated planning-review provider.
